metadata.description: Hawaiʻi assistance programs. Every fact has a verbatim quote from an official government or agency web page. scripts/verify_programs.py re-fetches each source and checks every quote; date_verified is the date that check last passed. Income figures are included only where the source page states them; otherwise they are left out.
metadata.framing: These are program descriptions, not eligibility decisions. People may qualify; only the administering agency can decide. Confirm with the agency.

source_domain_notes.hawaiipublicschools.org: Official site of the Hawaiʻi State Department of Education.
source_domain_notes.elderlyaffairs.com: Official site of the City and County of Honolulu Elderly Affairs Division (the Oʻahu Area Agency on Aging).

programs.name: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)
programs.agency: Hawaiʻi Department of Human Services, Benefit, Employment & Support Services Division (BESSD)
programs.agency_quote: In Hawaii, this service is provided by the Department of Human Services (DHS) Benefit, Employment & Support Services Division (BESSD).

serves.text: Food and nutrition support for qualifying low-income households.
serves.quote: The SNAP program provides crucial food and nutritional support to qualifying low-income and needy households, and those making the transition from welfare to self-sufficiency.

eligibility_factors.factor: Households must meet eligibility requirements and provide proof of household circumstances.
eligibility_factors.quote: Households must meet specific eligibility requirements and provide proof of their statements about household circumstances.

eligibility_factors.factor: U.S. citizens and some lawful permanent residents may qualify.
eligibility_factors.quote: U.S. citizens and some aliens who are admitted for permanent residency may qualify.

eligibility_factors.factor: Household income is compared with federal poverty level standards; the agency's chart is for reference only and an intake worker makes the final determination.
eligibility_factors.quote: This Federal Poverty Limit (FPL) chart is for reference only. An intake worker will make the final determination of your eligibility category.

income_standards.note: Published reference standards. An intake worker assigns the applicable standard and makes the final determination.

application.how: Apply online, by mail, or in person at a DHS processing center. Information line: 1-855-643-1643.
quotes: Apply online using the new ONLINE APPLICATION
For more information call Public Assistance Toll Free Information Line at 1-855-643-1643.

programs.name: Med-QUEST (Hawaiʻi Medicaid)
programs.agency: Hawaiʻi Department of Human Services, Med-QUEST Division
programs.agency_quote: The Med-QUEST Division accepts applications for medical assistance coverage online, over the phone, by mail or Fax.

serves.text: Medicaid health coverage, with programs for adults, children, parents and caretakers, pregnant people, and aged, blind or disabled individuals.
serves.quote: Your caseworker will help you find the Medicaid programs that fit your personal situation.

eligibility_factors.factor: A program for adults age nineteen or older and under age sixty-five.
eligibility_factors.quote: Provides Medicaid eligibility for individuals age nineteen years or older and under age sixty-five years.

eligibility_factors.factor: A program for infants and children under age nineteen (or under twenty-one in foster care, kinship guardianship or adoption assistance).
eligibility_factors.quote: Provides Medicaid eligibility for infants and children under age nineteen, or under age twenty one years old and in receipt of foster care, kinship guardianship, or adoption assistance.

eligibility_factors.factor: A program for a parent or caretaker relative living with a child under age nineteen.
eligibility_factors.quote: Provides Medicaid eligibility for a parent or other caretaker relative living with a child under age nineteen years.

eligibility_factors.factor: A program for aged, blind and disabled individuals.
eligibility_factors.quote: Provides Medicaid eligibility for aged, blind, and disabled individuals under the provisions of Title XIX of the Social Security Act.

application.how: Apply online through KOLEA, by phone, by mail or by fax.
quotes: The Med-QUEST Division accepts applications for medical assistance coverage online, over the phone, by mail or Fax.

programs.name: Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants and Children (WIC)
programs.agency: Hawaiʻi State Department of Health, WIC Services Branch
programs.agency_quote: Hawaii WIC clinics are operated under the auspices of the Hawaii WIC Services Branch of the Hawaii State Department of Health.

serves.text: Supplemental foods, nutrition education and referrals for pregnant, breastfeeding or postpartum women and children under five.
serves.quote: The participants of WIC are either pregnant, breastfeeding, or postpartum women, and infants and children under age five who meet income guidelines and have a medical or nutritional risk.

eligibility_factors.factor: Must be pregnant, breastfeeding or postpartum, or have children under 5 with nutritional needs; meet federal income guidelines; and live in Hawaiʻi.
eligibility_factors.quote: To qualify for Hawaii WIC services you must be either a pregnant, breastfeeding, or postpartum woman, or have children under 5 years old who have nutritional needs, meet federal income guidelines and be a resident of Hawaii.

eligibility_factors.factor: People with proof of QUEST, TANF or SNAP benefits meet WIC's income requirement.
eligibility_factors.quote: Individuals with proof of Quest or TANF benefit documents or food stamps meet WIC income eligibility requirements.

application.how: Contact a Hawaiʻi WIC clinic; local WIC agency staff determine eligibility.
quotes: To qualify for Hawaii WIC services you must be either a pregnant, breastfeeding, or postpartum woman

programs.name: Hawaiʻi Home Energy Assistance Program (H-HEAP, Hawaiʻi's LIHEAP)
programs.agency: Hawaiʻi Department of Human Services; applications handled by each island's Community Action Agency
programs.agency_quote: Applications for H-HEAP are only accepted and processed by Community Action Agency that serves your island.

serves.text: A one-time payment toward an eligible household's electric or gas bill.
serves.quote: The Hawai`i Home Energy Assistance Program (H-HEAP) provides heating and/or cooling assistance to eligible Hawai`i households by assisting with a one-time payment towards their electric or gas bill.

eligibility_factors.factor: Energy Crisis Intervention helps households whose electric or gas service has been or will be disconnected (with a disconnect notice); accepted year-round but monthly approvals are limited.
eligibility_factors.quote: Energy Crisis Intervention (ECI) assists needy households in crisis, the electric or gas service has been or will be disconnected, as the household has been notified via a disconnect notice from the utility company.

eligibility_factors.factor: Energy Credit applications are accepted only in June.
eligibility_factors.quote: Applications for EC will only accepted from June 1 - June 30.

eligibility_factors.factor: One type of H-HEAP payment per program year (October 1 to September 30).
eligibility_factors.quote: Households may only receive one type of H-HEAP payment per program year which runs from October 1 - September 30:

application.how: Apply through the Community Action Agency for your island, not DHS offices.
quotes: Applications for H-HEAP are only accepted and processed by Community Action Agency that serves your island.

programs.name: Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) and Temporary Assistance for Other Needy Families (TAONF)
programs.agency: Hawaiʻi Department of Human Services, Benefit, Employment & Support Services Division
programs.agency_quote: Temporary Assistance for Needy Families or TANF Program is a federal-funded block grant program that provides temporary cash assistance to eligible families that include at least one specified relative adult and a minor dependent child who resides in the same home.

serves.text: Temporary monthly cash assistance for families with a minor child living with a related adult. TAONF serves families not eligible for TANF because of citizenship status.
serves.quote: provides temporary cash assistance to eligible families that include at least one specified relative adult and a minor dependent child who resides in the same home.

eligibility_factors.factor: The family must include a related adult and a minor dependent child living in the same home.
eligibility_factors.quote: eligible families that include at least one specified relative adult and a minor dependent child who resides in the same home.

eligibility_factors.factor: TAONF covers families who would otherwise qualify but are not eligible for TANF because of citizenship status.
eligibility_factors.quote: to provide cash assistance to families that would have been eligible for benefits through the former AFDC Program but are not eligible through the TANF Program due to their citizenship status.

eligibility_factors.factor: Monthly gross income must be below 185% of the 2006 federal poverty level ($2,941 for a family of three), and adjusted net income below 100% of the 2006 level ($1,590 for a family of three).
eligibility_factors.quote: To qualify, a family's monthly gross income must be below 185% of the 2006 Federal Poverty level (FPL) or $2,941 for a family of three, and the adjusted net income must be below 100% of the 2006 FPL or $1,590 for the same family size.

eligibility_factors.factor: Lifetime limit of 60 months of cash assistance.
eligibility_factors.quote: Families may receive no more than sixty (60) months of cash assistance benefits in their lifetime through the TANF or TAONF Program.

eligibility_factors.factor: Families must take part in the First-To-Work Program.
eligibility_factors.quote: As a condition of eligibility, TANF and TAONF recipient families are required to participate with the First-To-Work Program.

application.how: Apply online through the Public Assistance Information System or with the DHS 1240 paper form.

programs.name: Housing Choice Voucher Program (Section 8), Hawaiʻi Public Housing Authority
programs.agency_quote: The HPHA provides rental assistance to low-income families in the private rental market through the Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) Program which is funded by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.

serves.text: Rental assistance for low-income families renting in the private market. The HPHA program covers Oʻahu only.
serves.quote: The HPHA provides rental assistance to low-income families in the private rental market through the Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) Program which is funded by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.

eligibility_factors.factor: The HPHA voucher program covers the island of Oʻahu only.
eligibility_factors.quote: The HPHA's HCV Program covers the island of Oahu only.

eligibility_factors.factor: Eligibility is based on annual gross income; whether the applicant is elderly, has a disability, or is a family; and U.S. citizenship or eligible immigration status.
eligibility_factors.quote: The HPHA determines your eligibility based on annual gross income; whether an applicant qualifies as elderly, a person with a disability, or as a family; and U.S. citizenship or eligible immigration status.

eligibility_factors.factor: HUD defines low-income families as earning 50% or less of the area median income.
eligibility_factors.quote: Low-income families are defined by HUD as earning 50% or less of the median income for a given county or metropolitan area.

time_sensitive.note: When verified, the HPHA said all waiting lists for this program were closed.
time_sensitive.quote: All waiting lists for this program are currently closed. Please check back later.

application.how: Online pre-application when a waiting list is open.
quotes: The HPHA's Housing Choice Voucher program (a.k.a. Section 8) on Oahu uses an online pre-application form.

programs.name: Free and Reduced-Price School Meals (National School Lunch Program)
programs.agency: Hawaiʻi State Department of Education, School Food Services Branch
programs.agency_quote: The program is administered locally by the Department’s School Food Services Branch.

serves.text: Free or low-cost school meals for children in public schools.
serves.quote: It provides nutritionally balanced, low-cost or free lunches to children each school day.

eligibility_factors.factor: For school year 2026-27, free meals extend to families with household incomes at or below 300% of the federal poverty level (Act 139, SLH 2025).
eligibility_factors.quote: Effective for the school year 2026-27, the Department has expanded its free meal eligibility to families with household incomes at or below 300% of the federal poverty level (ALICE households) under Act 139 (Session Laws of Hawaiʻi 2025).

eligibility_factors.factor: Eligible students receive one free breakfast and one free lunch each school day.
eligibility_factors.quote: Eligible students will receive one free breakfast and one free lunch each school day.

quotes: To submit an application for Free and Reduced-Price Meal Benefits, please visit EZMealApp.

programs.name: Kūpuna Care
programs.agency: Hawaiʻi Executive Office on Aging, through county Area Agencies on Aging (on Oʻahu, the City and County of Honolulu Elderly Affairs Division)
programs.agency_quote: Administered by: County Area Agencies on Aging (e.g., Elderly Affairs Division on O'ahu).

serves.text: Community-based long-term care services that help older adults keep living at home.
serves.quote: Kupuna Care is state/county funding designed to provide designed to provide community-based long-term care services to older adults with the goals of remaining at home for as long as possible.

eligibility_factors.factor: Age 60 or older.
eligibility_factors.quote: Age Requirement: 60 years or older.

eligibility_factors.factor: Must be a Hawaiʻi resident.
eligibility_factors.quote: Residency: Must be a Hawai'i resident.

eligibility_factors.factor: Must have functional needs (limits in daily activities) and not qualify for Medicaid or comparable programs.
eligibility_factors.quote: Eligibility: Must have functional needs (frailty or limitations in activities of daily living [ADLs] and/or instrumental activities of daily living [IADLs]). Does not qualify for Medicaid or other comparable programs.

eligibility_factors.factor: Cost-sharing may apply based on income; most services have waitlists.
eligibility_factors.quote: Cost: Cost-sharing may apply, based on income and ability to pay.

time_sensitive.note: When verified, the Elderly Affairs Division said most services have waitlists.

application.how: On Oʻahu, call the Senior Helpline at (808) 768-7700. On other islands, contact the county Area Agency on Aging (see the Hawaiʻi ADRC).
quotes: Call the Senior Helpline at (808) 768-7700 to get started.

programs.name: Veterans benefits help, Hawaiʻi Office of Veterans' Services (OVS)
programs.agency: Hawaiʻi Department of Defense, Office of Veterans' Services; federal benefits from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
programs.agency_quote: Advocacy is the primary service offered by the office. OVS may take action on behalf of Veterans, their families, and survivors to secure appropriate rights, benefits, & services.

serves.text: Advocacy and help with VA claims for veterans, their families and survivors, plus state benefits such as home tax exemptions for totally disabled veterans.
serves.quote: Advocacy is the primary service offered by the office. OVS may take action on behalf of Veterans, their families, and survivors to secure appropriate rights, benefits, & services.

eligibility_factors.factor: OVS helps prepare VA claims.
eligibility_factors.quote: Assist in preparation of VA claims

eligibility_factors.factor: People not qualified for VA benefits are referred to other agencies.
eligibility_factors.quote: Refer individuals not qualified for VA benefits to other agencies

eligibility_factors.factor: Real property tax exemptions for a home owned and occupied by a totally disabled veteran or their widow(er); varies by island.
eligibility_factors.quote: Tax exemptions on real property owned and occupied as a home by a totally disabled Veteran or their widow(er).

application.how: Contact OVS for help with a VA claim, or apply for federal benefits with the VA.

programs.name: Child Care Subsidy
programs.agency: Hawaiʻi Department of Human Services, Child Care Program
programs.agency_quote: The Child Care Subsidy program helps low-income families to sustain their employment, educational efforts and job training by paying a subsidy for their children who are in the care of DHS-approved child care providers.

serves.text: Help paying for child care so low-income parents can work, go to school or train.
serves.quote: The Child Care Subsidy program helps low-income families to sustain their employment, educational efforts and job training by paying a subsidy for their children who are in the care of DHS-approved child care providers.

eligibility_factors.factor: Child under 13 (or 13 to 18 if unable to do self care).
eligibility_factors.quote: Child: Under 13 years, or between 13 to 18 years if the child cannot do self care and resides with their parent(s) or caretakers;

eligibility_factors.factor: Parents or caretakers must be working, in school, or in job training.
eligibility_factors.quote: Parents or Caretakers: Must be employed, attending school, or participating in a job-training program.

eligibility_factors.factor: Gross monthly income must not exceed 85% of the State Median Income for the family size.
eligibility_factors.quote: Income limits by family size: Gross monthly income (before taxes and deductions) must not exceed 85% of the State Median Income for the family size.

application.how: Apply online or with the DHS 911 paper form.
